assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential account of how trade, technology, and changing task demand reshape employment and inequality, combining clear empirical evidence with a framework that has altered labour-economics research.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Hanson, and Katz are central to the distinct empirical and conceptual advances represented by this contribution.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been extensively studied, have shaped public and scholarly debate, and their implications have matured over a long period.
uncertainties: The contribution joins several related mechanisms, making the boundaries of a single prize-worthy discovery somewhat broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and supplied a powerful empirical basis for studying inequality of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman have especially clear credit for developing and applying this research programme.
assessment.maturity: The measurement innovations and substantive findings have been widely adopted and tested across locations and research questions.
uncertainties: The literature involves a broad collaborative network, so the most complete allocation of individual credit remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs made discrimination measurable through persuasive field evidence and have had enduring influence on labour-market research and policy.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are central architects of the modern influential audit-study approach in economics.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a substantial subsequent literature across countries and markets.
uncertainties: Interpretation of correspondence-study estimates can depend on the precise channel through which employers infer applicant characteristics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel methods supplied foundational tools for credible empirical work where persistence, unobserved heterogeneity, and endogeneity are central.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell, and Bond are directly and recognizably associated with the core methodological advances.
assessment.maturity: These methods have been standard tools for decades across applied economics.
uncertainties: The contribution is technical and its boundaries overlap with wider developments in instrumental-variables and GMM estimation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions and skill formation established that childhood environments have durable economic consequences, changing how economists study human capital and policy.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha made complementary and central contributions to evidence and dynamic interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The central insights are well established and have motivated a large empirical literature.
uncertainties: The programme encompasses several causal designs and mechanisms rather than one narrowly delimited discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony provided a durable framework for understanding wage setting and labour-market power, with major implications for minimum-wage and competition policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning has particularly clear intellectual credit for the modern monopsony framework.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has become central to contemporary labour economics and has gained extensive empirical relevance.
uncertainties: The ballot groups foundational theory with later empirical and policy-oriented work whose relative credit is less clear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression opened systematic analysis of heterogeneous relationships across outcome distributions and has become an indispensable empirical method.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett have unambiguous foundational credit for quantile regression.
assessment.maturity: The method is mature, widely used, and has generated extensive theoretical and applied development.
uncertainties: Its broad methodological impact may be judged less unified with later distributional extensions listed on the ballot.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice modelling made forward-looking individual decision problems empirically tractable and deeply influenced structural applied work.
assessment.attribution: Rust and Keane are leading contributors to the foundational modelling and estimation programme.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been influential for decades in labour, industrial organisation, and public economics.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed across a larger body of researchers, and computational assumptions can affect empirical conclusions.
